title: Key-grant routing and epoch rotation signalling
goal: Route `key.grant` events to the right devices without reading them, validate their routing metadata, and signal key epoch changes with `control.rotate_key` so removed members cannot read new frames.
scope_in: Validation of `key.grant` frames (hybrid): sender role host or editor, `p.to_device` is a device of a current member of this session, `p.kids` non-empty (<= 200, each matching `k<digits>`), no kid greater than the session's current epoch + 1.
Sequenced broadcast of valid grants through the normal pipeline (all members receive every sequenced frame so `seq` stays contiguous; only `to_device` can open the sealed boxes).
Epoch tracker per session: `current_kid` (starts `k1`), epoch start time and frame count since rotation; persisted in Redis `relay:ses:{sid}:epoch`.
`EpochSignal.rotate(sid, reason)`: emits server `control.rotate_key {kid:'k<e+1>', reason}` through B044 `emitServer`; reasons limited to `member_removed`, `scheduled`, `requested`.
Enforcement: after a member has acked a `rotate_key` seq, encrypted frames from that member with an older `ct.kid` are rejected; frames with a newer-than-current kid are rejected.

Detection of a rotation commit: a `key.grant` from the host whose `p.kids` contains `k<current+1>` advances the epoch and triggers `rotate_key` (reason `requested`, or `scheduled` if the 7 d / 100 000 frame trigger was due).
Scheduled-rotation due flag: when an epoch is 7 days old or has 100 000 frames, `EpochTracker.due()` reports `scheduled` and a metric is set; the relay never rotates by itself (the host decides).
scope_out: Sealing, opening or generating keys (client side, CT-CRYPTO).
Verifying `sig` on frames (optional abuse filter, not in v1 scope here).
build_against: The mock client simulator from B011 (scripted fake clients speaking the WS protocol), the in-memory B009 KV/pub-sub implementations, and the frame fixtures in contracts/fixtures/events/; no real client is needed. Grants use fixture contracts/fixtures/events/key.grant.json with random-byte sealed blobs; epoch behaviour is driven by simulator clients that rotate and send old-kid frames.
interfaces: TS: `interface EpochTracker { current(sid: string): Promise<{ kid: string; epoch: number; startedAt: string; framesSince: number }>; advance(sid: string, toKid: string): Promise<void>; due(sid: string): Promise<'none' | 'scheduled'> }`
TS: `interface EpochSignal { rotate(sid: string, reason: 'member_removed' | 'scheduled' | 'requested'): Promise<{ seq: number; kid: string }> }`
TS: `validateKeyGrant(frame: InboundFrame, ctx: { room: Room; epoch: EpochInfo }): { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: 'forbidden' | 'invalid_frame' }`
TS: `export default relayModule: RelayModule` (order 25) (validation before sequencing) and exposes `ctx.epoch`.
acceptance: A `key.grant` from an editor with `to_device` of a device that belongs to a member of the session and `kids:['k1']` is sequenced and delivered to all members with `p` and `ct` byte-identical; from a viewer it is rejected `forbidden`.
A grant addressed to a device that is not in the session, or with `kids` empty, containing `k0`, `kx`, or more than 200 entries, is rejected `invalid_frame` and not sequenced.

`EpochSignal.rotate(sid,'member_removed')` emits `control.rotate_key {kid:'k2',reason:'member_removed'}` with a `seq` directly after the preceding frame, and a following `rotate` yields `k3`; reasons outside the three allowed values throw.
When called right after a kick emission, the two frames carry consecutive seq numbers (test with a concurrent flood of 100 frames/s: kick+rotate remain adjacent).

After member M has acked the `rotate_key` seq, M sending an encrypted frame with `ct.kid:'k1'` gets `sys.error` `invalid_frame` and the frame is not sequenced; a frame sent before M's ack with the old kid is accepted (in-flight tolerance).
A frame with `ct.kid:'k9'` while current is `k2` is rejected.
A host `key.grant` with `kids:['k2']` when current is `k1` advances the epoch to `k2` and emits exactly one `rotate_key`; a second identical grant does not emit another.
`due()` returns `scheduled` once an epoch is 7 days old or has 100 000 frames, and the metric `relay_epoch_rotation_due` is set; the relay does not rotate by itself.
tests: keys.grant-validation.test.ts: role, target device, kids rules, fixture.
keys.stale-kid.test.ts: ack-based enforcement and in-flight tolerance.
keys.opaque.test.ts: grant `ct` is never parsed or logged (canary bytes).
keys.due.test.ts: 7 d and 100 000 frame triggers with fake clock.
guardrails: The relay MUST NOT choose, generate, hold or see keys; it only routes sealed grants and signals epochs. For `control.kick` the relay triggers rotation but never picks key material (CT-CRYPTO section 5).
`key.grant` `ct` and `sig` MUST be forwarded byte-identical and never logged; the clear `p` (`to_device`, `kids`) is the only part read.
`control.rotate_key` MUST be emitted only by the server; a client-sent one is rejected (B043) and MUST NOT be able to bump the epoch.
Stale-kid enforcement MUST be based on the member's acked seq, otherwise legitimate in-flight frames are lost.
Epoch state MUST survive relay restarts (Redis), otherwise a restart would accept stale epochs.
failure_modes: Epoch store unavailable -> grants and encrypted frames are rejected 503-class (fail closed) rather than skipping kid checks.
Host disconnected when rotation is needed -> rotate is still signalled by the caller (kick path) but session pausing is B053/B051's job.
Grant for a device that left between validation and delivery -> delivered anyway (sealed to a key only that device holds); no harm.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: no client->relay frame exists to request a non-kick rotation (CT-CRYPTO says the relay emits `rotate_key` after the host publishes grants for the next epoch); this card treats a host `key.grant` with the next kid as the commit signal. Scheduled rotation is the host's job (every 7 days or 100 000 frames); the relay only exposes `due()`.
